learning_outcomes.text: Master the basic operating principles of low-frequency broadband amplifiers. Analyze and compare different amplifier configurations. Study the effects of frequency on the transistor model.
Handle analog electronic circuit simulation tools.
Deepen knowledge and analysis of the main linear and non-linear applications of the operational amplifier. Design transfer functions.
Describe the integrated circuit manufacturing process.
Understand the internal structure of the operational amplifier: differential stages, current mirrors and sources, output stages.
Characteristics of the real operational amplifier as a circuit element: static characteristics, dynamic characteristics, and stability.
Other general-purpose analog integrated circuits: voltage regulators, variable voltage references, etc.
Perform simulation of general-purpose electronic circuits with computer tools.
Analyze the operation of a wide variety of electronic circuits that use idealized operational amplifiers.
Synthesize filters with discrete elements, both passive and active (based on operational amplifiers).

Understand the functions of the different electronic subcircuits (current sources and mirrors, differential stages, coupling stages, output stages, and protections) that configure the internal structure of an operational amplifier.
Understand and quantify how the actual internal structure of an operational amplifier modifies its idealized behavior.
Quantify how the real characteristics of an operational amplifier modify its behavior in circuits and establish comparisons with calculations obtained assuming ideal behavior.
Understand the operation of other general-purpose analog integrated circuits and their application in communications and power electronics.

syllabus_topics: Amplifier in common emitter, common collector and common base.
Amplifier in common source and common drain.
Effect of frequency on the transistor model.
Basic linear and non-linear circuits with ideal operational amplifiers.
Synthesis of filters with passive elements.
teaching_methods: Expositive classes (lectures) with PowerPoint presentations and whiteboard developments.
Aula practices for solving complex problems and acquiring circuit analysis skills.
Laboratory practices for practical illustration and construction of small electronic circuits.
Simulation practices for handling analog electronic circuit simulation tools.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance to Group Tutorial (TG) on IC manufacturing

assessment_rules: The final theoretical block grade is calculated as: Theory = ((0.125 x EP1) + (0.175 x EP2) + (0.6 x EF1) + (0.1 x T)) x TG, where TG is 0 for non-attendance and 1 for attendance (or justified work). The final practical block grade is calculated as: Practices = (0.5 x PL1) + (0.5 x PL2). The final course grade for the ordinary call is: Final = ((5 x Theory) + (Practices)) / 6. No minimum grade is required for individual evaluable components. In the extraordinary call, the practical grade is retained, and the theoretical block is evaluated by a single final exam (EF2), with the formula: Final = ((5 x EF2) + (Practices)) / 6. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is: Final = ((5 x ET) + EPL) / 6, where ET is a final theoretical exam and EPL is a practical exam.
